To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TBLT has more positive impact on L2 acquisition than TSLT in the case of the prepositions and declination of cases and verbs of motion.

(1) the acquisition of prepositions and case forms is not affected by the type of instruction, but the acquisition of motion verbs is affected positively by the type of task used; (2) in the written task, syntactic complexity measured by T-units and lexical complexity increases significantly after the instruction, but there were no significant improvements in syntactic complexity in the oral task; (3) accuracy improved significantly in both groups in the post-test immediately after the instruction, and in the post-test

the students in both groups improved their performance on the grammaticality judgment test, their accuracy on the written task, and their fluency and accuracy on the oral task, while their complexity did not increase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact on L2 acquisition of two different types of task-based language teaching: TSLT and TBLT.
comparing the effectiveness of TSLT (task supported language teaching) and TBLT (task based language teaching) in the acquisition of Russian as a foreign language.

the impact of two types of language teaching methodology on the acquisition of the Russian language by Spanish learners: TSLT (task supported language teaching) and TBLT (task based language teaching).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the students who participated in the study improved significantly in their knowledge and use of Russian prepositions and declination, but did not show any significant improvement in their knowledge and production of verbs of motion.

the TBLT methodology is more successful than TSLT in the acquisition of Russian as a foreign language, but the results of the study should be considered as preliminary, as the sample is not big enough.
the TBLT methodology is the most effective for the acquisition of Russian as a foreign language, especially in terms of lexical complexity and verb movement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained show that TBLT is a more effective approach to the acquisition of Russian as a foreign language than TSLT, especially in the case of the acquisition of verbs of movement.

the results show that the students of the TBLT group have improved their competence in the use of verbs of motion in both oral and written production, while the students of the FOF group have improved their grammatical competence in the use and declination of prepositions and cases.
the students who received task based instruction showed better results than those who received focus on forms instruction, especially in the acquisition of verbs of movement and lexical complexity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both TSLT and TBLT can be used to teach Russian as an FL and that both approaches can be effective.
the task based approach to language teaching is superior in its ability to foster the acquisition of the target language.
the use of tasks in the teaching of Russian as a foreign language is beneficial for the acquisition of the Russian language.
